'''Richard Keith Ellis''', {{Post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|FRS}} (born 17 November 1949) is a British [[theoretical physicist]], working at the [[University of Durham]], and a leading authority on perturbative [[Quantum Chromodynamics|quantum chromodynamics]] and collider phenomenology.

==Education==
Ellis graduated from the [[University of Oxford]] (MA 1971, D.Phil. 1974). He has held positions at [[Imperial College]], [[MIT]], [[Caltech]], [[CERN]] and the [[Sapienza University of Rome|University of Rome]].

==Career and research==
Ellis went to [[Fermilab]] in 1984 and was Head of the Theoretical Physics Department there from 1993 to 2004. In 2015 he moved to the [[University of Durham]] in the UK, where he was a professor of Physics and Director of the Institute for Particle Physics Phenomenology until the end of 2019.

Ellis' work is of importance to the study of elementary particles at colliders, such as the Fermilab Tevatron, and the CERN [[Large Hadron Collider]]. Ellis has contributed in a substantial way to the interpretation of experiments performed at high energy. Together with Douglas Ross and Tony Terrano he performed the first calculation of jet structure in e+e- annihilation which allowed precise determination of the strong coupling.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=R.Keith Ellis |author2=D.A. Ross |author3=A.E. Terrano | title=The Perturbative Calculation of Jet Structure in e+ e- Annihilation
| journal=Nuclear Physics
| volume=B178 | issue=3 | pages=421–456 | year=1981 | doi=10.1016/0550-3213(81)90165-6|bibcode = 1981NuPhB.178..421E }}</ref>
In addition, with Guido Altarelli and Guido Martinelli he performed a calculation of lepton pair production which allow reconciliation of observed rates with theoretical calculations.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Guido Altarelli |author2=R.Keith Ellis |author3=G. Martinelli | title=Large Perturbative Corrections to the Drell-Yan Process in QCD
| journal=Nuclear Physics| volume=B157 | pages=461–497 |issue=3 | year=1979 | doi=10.1016/0550-3213(79)90116-0|bibcode = 1979NuPhB.157..461A }}</ref>
He has also co-authored a number of widely read papers on the theory of heavy quark production.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=P. Nason, S. Dawson  |author2=R. Keith Ellis
| name-list-style=amp | title=The Total Cross-Section for the Production of Heavy Quarks in Hadronic Collisions
| journal=Nuclear Physics| volume=B303 | pages=607–633 | issue=4 | year=1988
| doi=10.1016/0550-3213(88)90422-1|bibcode = 1988NuPhB.303..607N }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=P. Nason, S. Dawson  |author2=R. Keith Ellis
| name-list-style=amp | title=The One Particle Inclusive Differential Cross-Section for Heavy Quark Production in Hadronic Collisions
| journal=Nuclear Physics| volume=B327 | pages=49–92 | issue=1 | year=1989
| doi=10.1016/0550-3213(89)90286-1|bibcode = 1989NuPhB.327...49N |s2cid=122981606
}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=John C. Collins  |author2=R. Keith Ellis
| name-list-style=amp | title=Heavy quark production in very high-energy hadron collisions
| journal=Nuclear Physics| volume=B360 |issue=1
| pages=3–30 | year=1991
| doi=10.1016/0550-3213(91)90288-9|bibcode = 1991NuPhB.360....3C }}</ref>
He is also co-author for the parton-level Monte Carlo program MCFM.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Campbell|first1=John|last2=Ellis|first2=Keith|last3=Williams|first3=Ciaran|title=MCFM – Monte Carlo for FeMtobarn processes|url=http://mcfm.fnal.gov/|website=MCFM|publisher=Fermilab}}</ref>

Ellis is the coauthor with [[James Stirling (physicist)|W. J. Stirling]] and [[B. R. Webber]] of a book on QCD and collider physics published by Cambridge University Press in 1996.<ref>[https://inspirehep.net/author/profile/R.K.Ellis.1 Scientific publications of R. K. Ellis] on [[INSPIRE-HEP]]</ref>

==Honours and awards==
Ellis was elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1988 and a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] of London in 2009. Also in 2009, Ellis together with [[John C. Collins|John Collins]] and [[Davison Soper]] won the [[Sakurai Prize|J. J. Sakurai Prize for Theoretical Particle Physics]], ''For work in perturbative Quantum Chromodynamics, including applications to problems pivotal to the interpretation of high energy particle collisions.''<ref>[https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/sakurai.cfm American Physical Society – J. J. Sakurai Prize Winners]</ref> In 2019 he was awarded the [[Dirac Medal (IOP)|Paul Dirac Medal]] of the Institute of Physics,<ref>[https://www.iop.org/about/awards/gold-medals/paul-dirac-medal-and-prize-recipients Paul Dirac Medal and Prize recipients]</ref> ''For his seminal work in quantum chromodynamics (QCD) where he performed many of the key calculations that led to the acceptance of QCD as the correct theory of the strong interaction.''
